_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.text: Someone wrote the rules for sending internet traffic by pigeon.
beats.note: RFC 1149, by David Waitzman of BBN, dated 1 April 1990. The datagram is printed in hexadecimal on a paper scroll and wrapped round a leg with duct tape.
That is the RFC's own wording for the maximum size of a packet.

beats.name: Bergen Linux User Group
beats.role: Ran it for real in Norway on 28 April, with ping packets on pigeons' legs. They read the replies back with OCR software.

beats.context: Nine pings went out and four replies came back. The slowest round trip took 6,389 seconds.

beats.note: Their pigeons stayed to fly with the others for about an hour, and an open cage at the far end let more escape.

beats.text: The team still called it a success.

beats.line: Packet loss has a flight path.
